record.paper_title: Optimal scaling of average queue sizes in an input-queued switch: an open problem
record.original_question: When the load factor ρ is held fixed in the same input-queued switch setting, can a Markovian scheduling policy, whose action depends only on the current queue vector rather than the full past history, achieve steady-state expected total queue-size performance O(n^(1+ε)) for every ε > 0, matching the near-linear dependence in n suggested by batching policies without requiring a non-Markovian history-dependent rule?

evidence.quote: we conjecture this property to be true, so that Markovian policies can also deliver O(n1+ε) performance (for any ε > 0) when ρ is held fixed.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an n×n input-queued switch operating in discrete time. There are n input ports and n output ports, with a separate queue Q_{ij}(t) at each input i for packets destined to output j (so n^2 queues in total). At each time step t = 0, 1, 2, …:

1. Arrivals: independent Bernoulli arrivals occur at each (i,j) with rate λ_{ij}, where the arrival rate matrix Λ = (λ_{ij}) satisfies max_i ∑_j λ_{ij} ≤ ρ and max_j ∑_i λ_{ij} ≤ ρ for some load factor ρ ∈ (0,1).

2. Service: a scheduler chooses a matching M(t) (a permutation of {1,…,n}, identified with a perfect matching of the complete bipartite graph K_{n,n}); for every (i,j) in M(t), one packet (if any) is removed from Q_{ij}(t).

A scheduling policy is called Markovian if the matching M(t) is chosen as a (possibly randomized) function only of the current queue-length vector Q(t) = (Q_{ij}(t)), without using the history of past queue states, arrivals, or matchings.

Assume the system is stable and let E[∑_{i,j} Q_{ij}(∞)] denote the steady-state expected total queue size.

Question. Fix the load factor ρ ∈ (0,1). Does there exist a Markovian scheduling policy such that, for every ε > 0, the steady-state expected total queue size satisfies

   E[∑_{i,j} Q_{ij}(∞)] = O(n^{1+ε})    as n → ∞,

uniformly over all admissible arrival rate matrices with the given load ρ? Equivalently, can the near-linear-in-n queue scaling that batching-based (history-dependent) policies are known to achieve be matched by a policy whose action depends only on the current queue vector?
artifact.category_tag: queueing theory and scheduling in switched networks
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has substantially improved queue-size scaling bounds for input-queued switches. In particular, Xu and Zhong (2019/2020) introduced a scheduling policy based on graph factorization with steady-state expected total queue size O(n(1−ρ)^{−4/3} log max{1/(1−ρ), n}), which for fixed ρ gives O(n log n) and hence O(n^{1+ε}) for every ε>0. Related improved-delay-scaling results have appeared in Advances in Applied Probability (2020) and Queueing Systems (2021). However, these constructions typically rely on batching/frame-based ideas rather than purely Markovian (memoryless in the queue vector) rules, so the specific question of whether a Markovian policy can attain O(n^{1+ε}) for fixed ρ does not appear to be definitively settled in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: Improved queue-size scaling for input-queued switches via graph factorization
status_evidence.snippet: new class of scheduling policies under which the expected total queue size scales as O(n(1-ρ)^{-4/3} log(max{1/(1-ρ), n}))
status_evidence.claim: Achieves near-linear-in-n scaling for fixed ρ, but via a frame/batching-based policy.

status_evidence.title: Optimal queue-size scaling in switched networks
status_evidence.snippet: new class of online scheduling policies that achieve optimal queue-size scaling for input-queued switches
status_evidence.claim: Earlier batching-based policies attain near-optimal scaling, motivating the question of Markovian counterparts.

status_evidence.title: An algorithm for improved delay-scaling in input-queued switches
status_evidence.claim: Continued progress on delay/queue-size scaling, still relying on structured (non-purely-Markovian) algorithms.
